articles.title: FCC proposes clamping down on state and local broadband delays, debates E-Rate program
articles.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is actively addressing complaints from broadband providers. These concerns highlight how existing state and local regulations are reportedly hindering the smooth and efficient construction of crucial broadband infrastructure. The FCC's intervention aims to streamline deployment processes, which is vital for enhancing national connectivity and supporting economic development by reducing regulatory friction for essential service expansion.

articles.title: We tend to imagine the Moon as a barren, resourceless rock, but the permanently shadowed craters near its south pole hold something future astronauts may prize more than gold: water ice, confirmed by NASA missions, that could one day be split into oxygen to breathe and hydrogen for rocket fuel.
articles.summary: Initially viewed as a dry, inert body of dust and stone, the Moon's appearance from Earth and early Apollo samples reinforced this perception. However, scientific advancements are now challenging this simplistic view, revealing a potentially more complex and dynamic lunar environment. This ongoing research continues to redefine our understanding of Earth's closest celestial neighbor.

articles.title: US FCC toughens submarine communication cable rules
articles.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has voted to significantly toughen oversight of submarine communication cables, which carry 99% of all international internet traffic. New rules are proposed to enhance security and scrutiny of these vital undersea links. This move underscores the critical importance of securing global digital infrastructure, impacting international data flow and cybersecurity, a growing strategic concern.

articles.title: Colonel, major named in FIR over alleged attack on J&K's Kishtwar police station
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Police have registered a case against several Army men from the 17 Rashtriya Rifles in Kishtwar district. The soldiers are accused of allegedly barging into a police station and assaulting officers. This serious incident, involving civil and military personnel, highlights potential inter-agency issues and warrants a thorough investigation into discipline and conduct in the sensitive region.
